static_traits.name: Chen Diane
static_traits.educational_background: Studies at a well-known fashion design school
static_traits.family_status: Moved to New York alone for school
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with classmates are tense due to self-criticism; although a few classmates can communicate, it is hard to openly talk about self-critical thoughts
static_traits.medical_history: History: no similar psychological problems yet; no counseling or treatment received yet; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, Good logic; able to describe emotions and thoughts specifically; highly cooperative, Positive attitude; but tending to focus on negative feedback and negate positive achievements

basic_info.main_problem: Even with 5 A's and 1 B, I still feel I am a 'bad Student', developing helplessness and self-criticism; these thoughts appear after every academic evaluation and affect self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these negative thoughts are affecting my motivation and passion for fashion design.

core_beliefs: I am not as good as my classmates

special_situations.event: Checks final exam results (5 A's and 1 B)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If grades are not perfect (e.g., not all A's), it means I am not good enough/a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on negative grades for self-criticism; tries to use rational reminders of own achievements to offset negative thoughts; reduces interaction with classmates to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a bad Student; one B proves I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Received feedback on a design project (overall positive, but color-scheme issues were pointed out)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If criticized in one aspect, it means overall ability is insufficient and I am not suited for this field
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Treating single-point criticism as an overall ability deficit and doubling self-reproach; Social withdrawal to avoid further negative evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot even handle colors well; I should not be here

special_situations.event: Getting an A grade or receiving positive feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good results are just luck and cannot show I really have ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating and belittling positive achievements to prevent 'complacency', continuing to emphasize shortcomings to 'push' oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is just luck; anyone could get an A

special_situations.event: Each time receiving academic assessment (grades or mentor evaluations)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach my classmates' level, I do not deserve to be around them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeps distance from classmates and reduces communication, avoiding being compared and evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never measure up to my classmates

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized, affirmed as a 'capable Student'
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being criticized and negated, fearing being seen as not good enough or not belonging in this field
defense_goal: Avoiding Anxiety and shame from outside evaluation through self-criticism and Social withdrawal

object_relations.self_representation: A student who is not good enough and prone to failure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving academic evaluations or criticism (such as negative feedback on color matching)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will see me as not good enough; these evaluations prove I am not suited for this field
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a steady, non-judgmental tone, first Empathy shame and Anxiety; then distinguish facts from speculation, invite specific evidence, and gently examine the basis for 'what others are thinking'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others emphasize one's achievements and strengths
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Rationally knowing there are achievements, but emotionally unable to believe or connect, feeling 'empty'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Warm tone, slowed pace; guide the identification of bodily sensations and emotion labels, encourage staying with and experiencing them (rather than only rational analysis), and use specific moments of success to carry out emotion focusing and grounding exercises.

manifestations: Moved to New York alone for school
Relationship tension with classmates and Social withdrawal
Finds it hard to open up to classmates about self-critical thoughts
When facing one's own achievements, feels 'briefly reassured but quickly hollow'
Hard to experience real value and self-recognition in positive feedback
outcomes: Learning motivation and passion for fashion design decline

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Feeling 'undeserving' in interactions with classmates, thus Withdrawal
Overly focuses on negative evaluations and ignores positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats 'must be perfect / get all A's' as the absolute standard for measuring self-worth
Treating single-point criticism as overall negate and internalizing it as self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: When facing criticism or comparison, not communicating needs and feelings with others, turning to harshness toward oneself
Social withdrawal, reducing communication with classmates to avoid being evaluated

exception_events.target_problem: When receiving academic evaluations, the client usually focuses only on the negative parts (such as a B or criticism), quickly developing Self-denial and a sense of failure, which then affects sleep, diet, and social life.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the moment of checking final grades that time, the client briefly felt happy and proud of the 5 A's, and did not immediately fall into self-criticism.
exception_events.reason: Different situation/understanding: first noticing the multiple A's and allowing oneself to acknowledge achievement; at the time catastrophic and filtering thinking had not yet occupied all attention, so a brief positive experience appeared.

positive_force: Has solid professional ability and skills (5 A's among the grades; work evaluated as 'innovative, technically solid')
Willing to seek help and participate in counseling; positive attitude
Can acknowledge and experience one's own achievements in brief moments
negative_force: Setting excessively high, rigid standards, viewing imperfection as failure
Mental filtering and overgeneralization, negating positive feedback
Self-criticism and Social withdrawal, reducing outside support
Anxiety and rumination triggered by academic evaluation, leading to Sleep and diet disturbance

target_behavior.behavior: Excessively focusing on negative academic feedback with Self-denial (repeated self-criticism and failure-oriented self-labels)
antecedent: Receiving project feedback from mentors / judges
target_behavior.core_reason: High standards for perfection and black-and-white evaluation, generalizing single-point negative information into overall not-good-enough
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the sense of failure and the possibility of being negated, trying to maintain a sense of control over progress through self-reproach
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-esteem, Study motivation impaired; Persistent anxiety and rumination, affecting sleep and diet

target_behavior.behavior: Social withdrawal and avoidance with classmates (reducing communication, feeling undeserving of being around classmates)
antecedent: Thinking of oneself as 'not as good as classmates' after grades or feedback
Occasions requiring discussing studies or presenting works with classmates
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and Self-doubt triggered by comparison and despair, worrying about being evaluated or exposing shortcomings
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of being compared and negatively evaluated, reducing Anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, Decreased support, rising Loneliness, further weakening self-confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep and diet patterns disturbed (difficulty falling asleep, appetite changes)
antecedent: After receiving academic evaluation, ruminates and self-criticizes
Anticipating negative outcomes when facing upcoming evaluations
target_behavior.core_reason: Persistent rumination and Anxiety activating physiological arousal, disrupting rhythms
target_behavior.function: Ineffective emotion-regulation attempts (trying to gain certainty through rumination)
target_behavior.consequence: Physical and mental exhaustion and declining concentration further affect academic performance and interpersonal interaction
